newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: DUIKER SUFFERS FROM LONRHO, JCI MERGER TALK.
newsitem.headline: DUIKER SUFFERS FROM LONRHO, JCI MERGER TALK.

text.p: Duiker Mining Ltd, a coal firm in the Lonrho Plc stable, shed recent share price gains on Tuesday amid continuing talks on an impending tie-up between Lonhro and JCI Ltd , dealers said.

They said that if the talks -- first made public last week -- on the possible merger of the two companies dragged on with no immediate outcome, the share could be plauged by some volatility, triggered by speculation.
"If this merger talk drags on longer you are more likely to see the share yo-yo up and down," one dealer said.

"This is all part and parcel of this JCI and Lonrho merger that's on the cards. Analysts are obviously putting value on it (Duiker) now and are identifying at what level it may go into JCI hence the share price moving lower," another dealer added.
Duiker shares had surged last week when Lonhro and JCI confirmed they were in talks and climbed seven percent or 70 cents to finish at 10.70 rand on Friday.
But on Tuesday the share lost ground and shed 46 cents to reach 954 cents at noon before recovering by 1310 GMT and was last unchanged at 10.00 rand with 40,000 shares having changed hands.

Dealer said last week the talks between Lonhro and JCI -- which recently enlarged its Tavistock coal division with the acquisition of Royal Dutch/Shell's South African coal business -- also included a possible tie-up of JCI's coal unit with Duiker.
"Everybody is vying for control of the coal stake of Lonrho," one dealer added.
South Africa's Business Day newspaper said last week that Avmin Ltd and Gencor Ltd were also interested in tying up with Lonrho.
Industry watchers say the possible merger between Lonrho and JCI could create a mining company with market capitalisation of more than $3 billion.
The Lonrho board was meeting on Tuesday to discuss JCI's merger proposals but no immediate announcement was expected, a Lonrho spokesman said in London.
